item.title: “Ghost preparers” tied to $179 million in potentially fraudulent refunds
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: A TIGTA report linked ghost preparers to $179 million in refund claims over two years. Its findings come as legislators consider the Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act, which would expand IRS oversight of paid tax return preparers.

item.title: AICPA: Trump account regulations make 2026 rollout difficult
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: Proposed regulations governing employer contributions to Trump accounts are “administratively burdensome” and make a 2026 rollout potentially difficult, the AICPA said. A letter to the IRS and Treasury asked for employers to be given more time and for the programs to be easier to administer.

item.title: Final regulations clear path for direct IRS card payments
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: The IRS on Friday issued final regulations implementing Taxpayer First Act provisions that would allow taxpayers to make credit and debit card tax payments directly to the IRS rather than through third-party payment processors. The final regulations adopt, without change, proposed regulations issued in July 2024.

item.title: IRS urged by national taxpayer advocate to pause Kwong claims denials
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: National Taxpayer Advocate Erin Collins urged the IRS to halt denials of claims tied to ongoing Kwong litigation, arguing that taxpayers could lose rights or pursue unnecessary litigation while courts continue to consider the case. The IRS has received more than 275,000 refund and abatement claims related to Kwong, she said.

item.title: IRS proposes regulations implementing premium tax credit changes
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: The IRS and Treasury proposed regulations implementing Sec. 36B premium tax credit changes enacted in H.R. 1, including new eligibility and verification requirements, reporting changes, and rules governing repayment of excess advance premium tax credits.

item.title: IRS grants Hurricane Isaias tax relief in Alabama, Florida
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: Taxpayers in parts of Alabama and Florida that sustained damage from Hurricane Isaias have until February to file various federal tax returns and make tax payments under disaster relief announced Wednesday by the IRS. The IRS said it will automatically identify taxpayers in the covered disaster areas and apply the relief.

item.title: Social Security wage base and COLA announced for 2027
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: The Social Security Administration announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment for 2027 and increased the Social Security wage base to $192,300. The annual update also includes changes to retirement earnings limits and other indexed Social Security amounts that affect taxpayers and employers.

item.title: AICPA recommends IRS clarification of Form 8050
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: The AICPA asked the IRS to clarify that Form 8050, used to provide direct deposit information for tax refunds, will not be included in exempt organizations' publicly available tax return filings. An AICPA letter said the change would reduce the risk of inadvertently disclosing sensitive banking information.

item.title: Treasury, IRS propose regulations for education tax credit
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: Treasury and the IRS proposed regulations for the education freedom tax credit, a new federal credit under Sec. 25F for contributions to organizations that provide scholarships to eligible elementary and secondary schools.

item.title: Senate approves taxpayer-focused reforms backed by AICPA
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: The Senate unanimously approved the Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act, a bipartisan package of 65 tax administration reforms backed by the AICPA. The measure now moves to the House.

item.title: IRS changes course to allow automatic Trump account enrollment
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: Treasury and the IRS issued proposed and temporary regulations providing for automatic enrollment in Trump accounts after developing a structure they said overcame barriers that previously stymied the move. Treasury estimated the approach could create more than 60 million additional accounts.

item.title: GAO tax fraud estimate puts annual losses at up to $304 billion
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: A first-of-its-kind GAO analysis estimates annual federal tax fraud losses at $116 billion to $304 billion. The report said that the IRS needs a coordinated antifraud strategy. The IRS partially agreed with the recommendations but disputed aspects of the report's methodology.

item.title: IRS launches mobile app with expanded account access
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: After 15 years as IRS2Go, the IRS’s taxpayer app now offers expanded access to account services under a new name. The IRS said it expects to add more capabilities to the app over time.

item.title: Identity theft victims waited 20 months for IRS case resolution
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: A TIGTA report found that IRS delays in resolving identity theft cases cost the government $124.2 million in refund interest from fiscal years 2023 through 2025. The findings echo warnings from National Taxpayer Advocate Erin Collins, who has called the wait times “unconscionable.”

item.title: IRS finalizes increase in estate tax closing letter fee
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: The IRS issued final regulations increasing the cost of an estate tax closing letter to $76 from $56, adopting without change proposed regulations issued in June.

item.title: IRS raises per diem rates for business travel effective Oct. 1
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: In its annual update, the IRS increased the special per diem rates taxpayers may use to substantiate business travel expenses for the upcoming travel year and updated its list of high-cost localities.

item.title: AICPA, former IRS commissioner to lead initiative on AI in tax
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: Participants in the Council on AI Risk in Tax, led by the AICPA and former IRS commissioner Danny Werfel, include leaders from all areas of the tax world who will work together to promote the responsible use of AI in tax administration and practice.

item.title: IRS cyber weaknesses put taxpayer data at risk again, TIGTA says
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: For the second consecutive year, a government watchdog found the IRS's cybersecurity program ineffective. TIGTA warned that taxpayer data could be vulnerable if security weaknesses are not addressed.

item.title: Unclear instructions, limited awareness plagued CP53E rollout, TIGTA says
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: Many CPAs and their clients experienced confusion over IRS CP53E notices during the 2026 filing season. A TIGTA report confirms those concerns and sheds new light on how the IRS implemented its paperless-payment initiative.

item.title: Government says Kwong court misread COVID tax relief law
item.dc:creator: By Martha Waggoner
item.description: In its opening brief to a federal appeals court Wednesday, the federal government said a lower court ruling in Kwong improperly turned a 60-day extension into a postponement period lasting over three years.
